Reinaldo Javier Aguiar Marcano
Application No. 19/574,352
Filed: 22 Mar 2026
For: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR SECURE ASYNCHRONOUS DATA COMMUNICATION
: DECISION ON PETITION

This is a decision on the “PETITION TO THE DIRECTOR UNDER 37 CFR § 1.183 TO SUSPEND PROSECUTION ON CONSTITUTIONAL DUE PROCESS AND NATIONAL DEFENSE GROUNDS [REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ADMINISTRATIVE PROCESSING]”, filed August 2, 2026.
The petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is DISMISSED.
Any request for reconsideration of this decision must be submitted within two (2) months from the mail date of this decision. Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are NOT available.

On March 22, 2026, Applicant filed the instant application. On July 8, 2026, the Office mailed a Notice to File Missing Parts of Nonprovisional Application. This Notice set an extendable period for reply of two months for Applicant to submit replacement claims (because Applicant’s claims did not commence on a separate sheet), and the statutory basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, surcharge for their late filing, and non-DOCX fee (Applicant paid the search fee, examination fee, and non-DOCX fee at the micro entity rate, but did not file a Certification of Micro Entity Status form).

On July 27, 2026, Applicant paid the $34 surcharge (micro entity rate) for late filing of the application filing fee. However, Applicant did not pay the balance of the basic filing fee, examination fee, or search fees still due at the small entity rate (or a Certification of Micro Entity Status form). Nor did Applicant file replacement claims. Accordingly, the Office mailed a Notice of Incomplete Reply on August 20, 2026.

On August 2, 2026, Applicant has filed the instant petition, requesting the Office suspend prosecution of the application because he is “currently legally and physical incapacitated from prosecuting this application or safely retaining patent counsel.” Specifically, Applicant requests suspension of 37 CFR 1.103(a)’s requirement that there be no outstanding Office action before the Office may grant a suspension of action.
37 CFR 1.183 states:

In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations in this part which is not a requirement of the statutes may be suspended or waived by the Director or the Director’s designee, sua sponte, or on petition of the interested party, subject to such other requirements as may be imposed. Any petition seeking a decision under this section must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(f).

Applicant has not shown that this is an extraordinary situation such that justice requires suspension or waiver of the rules. There is no need for a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to suspend or waive any rules because Applicant can purchase extensions of time to response to the Notice to File Missing Parts. The last day Applicant can respond to the Notice to File Missing Parts, with the maximum five month extension of time, is February 8, 2026. Here, Applicant has failed to explain why the available extensions of time are not sufficient to address his requested relief. Moreover, Applicant has failed to explain why his ongoing litigation activities prevent him from filing a response to the Notice to File Missing Parts and then requesting suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103.
The period for responding to the Notice to File Missing Parts mailed July 8, 2026 continues to run from the mail date of that Notice.
